settings.text: The bike was the first thing I ever made with my own hands. When my daughter rode it on family visit day, I felt like a dad again.
Pandas eat it. Schoolchildren used to be caned with it. But now prisoners at Lowdham Grange have found a surprising new use for bamboo — making bicycles out of it.
Bamboo bikes have that cool factor that excites them. There's maths and English in the programme — but it's built into design, creativity and bike mechanics.

settings.hero_lede: We use bamboo bike-building to give practical skills and a way forward to people locked out of education — in schools before exclusion, and in prisons after.
settings.arm1_body: Reaching SEND, PRU and at-risk young people before disengagement hardens into exclusion their first real, positive encounter with engineering and design.
settings.arm1_flow: start free :: the speaker build, 2–3 hours | choose a strand :: product, bicycle, additive or e-mobility | OCN accredited :: recognised skills, real qualifications | teachers run it :: film, session plan and curriculum map included
settings.arm2_body: Re-engaging people inside prison with accredited skills, a strengthened family bond, and a route towards employment on release.
settings.arm2_flow: six-week cohort :: six Makers, 18 hours a week | OCN Level 2 accredited :: workshop skills and sustainable manufacturing | a bike for their child :: handed over on family visit day | train as a peer instructor :: teach the next cohort | a route to work on release :: employer partners
settings.fork_label: STEM Education one mission, two pathways
settings.arm1_who: for secondary schools, sixth forms and colleges — five programmes, from a free classroom build to a rideable frame. curriculum-mapped, and built to be teacher-led.
settings.arm2_who: for people inside prison earning a hands-on manufacturing qualification — six-week Build to Bond cohorts at Lowdham Grange, Foston Hall, Lindholme and Feltham.
